notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1985:VI.5.9.5 GR6: 'The currency symbol must be the leftmost character position to be counted in the size of the item except that it can be preceded by either a '+' or a '-' symbol.' PictureComposition.Precedence gives a non-floating currency symbol two candidate roles at every edition, PicRole.CurrencyLeading and PicRole.CurrencyTrailing, and accepts the string when either satisfies Table10Rows; the trailing role is §2023:13.18.40.3 SR26's ('or the rightmost symbol in character-string-1, optionally followed by one of the symbols' + - CR DB), which §2002:13.16.38.2 SR23 already has and 1985 does not: the 1985 chart has one non-floating cs row, whose only x is under the leading {+ -}. Neither Precedence nor Validate reads the edition, so PIC 999$, +999$, 999$CR and 999$- compile at --std 85 and edit with the currency symbol last. The rest of the rule is implemented and edition-neutral: Validate refuses a second fixed currency symbol or sign symbol and two kinds of sign symbol (COBOL1934: $9$9, +999+, +999CR, 999CRDB); the walk refuses CR or DB anywhere but last and '+' or '-' anywhere but first or last (COBOL1935: CR999, 99DB9, 9+9, 99-99, $+999) and admits +$999 and -$999; CobolEdit.Render puts each insertion character at its own position, gives '+' as + or -, '-' as space or -, CR and DB as two spaces or the uppercase letters (PIC 999cr edits -3 to 003CR), all probed at --std 85. The witness runs +999, -999, $999CR and $999DB with both signs.

next.reason: 1985: 'The currency symbol must be the leftmost character position ... except that it can be preceded by either a '+' or a '-''. §2023:13.18.40.3 SR26 also allows it as 'the rightmost symbol in character-string-1, optionally followed by one of the symbols '+', '-', 'CR', or 'DB'', so PIC 999$ and 999$CR, refused in 1985, are accepted (looser). The one-symbol limits (§2023:13.18.40.3 SR23, SR24), sign position (§2023:13.18.40.3 SR25), CR/DB size (§2023:13.18.40.4 GR14) and the result table (§2023:13.18.40.5 GR5) are unchanged.
